d: Tumor suppressor genes whose proteins repair double-strand DNA breaks by homologous recombination; germline variants raise breast and ovarian cancer risk, and BRCA2 also raises male breast cancer risk.
Contractile cells that form the outer layer of breast ducts and lobules on the basement membrane; they persist around carcinoma in situ and are lost once a carcinoma invades.
A calcium-dependent adhesion protein encoded by CDH1 that holds epithelial cells together; its loss makes lobular carcinoma cells dyscohesive, so they grow in single file.
A crusted, eczematous nipple lesion caused by carcinoma cells that spread into the epidermis from an underlying ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive carcinoma.
A receptor tyrosine kinase encoded by ERBB2; gene amplification drives growth signaling in HER2-positive breast cancer and makes the tumor a target for trastuzumab and related drugs.
